title: 2026-03-18-shortlist-curation-and-compatibility-snapshot-greenline-health-demo
summary: Redwood AE+SE walk Greenline Health through a targeted shortlist workflow in the model catalog, a quick bench snapshot, and compatibility matrix guidance. Main themes: shortlist criteria, latency vs cost tradeoffs, on-prem vs hosted routing, and next steps to run a 2-week bench sprint with sample prompts and data residency constraints.
action_items: Ethan - share internal prompt set and 3 representative workflows by 2026-03-25
Marcus - provision bench template and cloud/runtime config doc by 2026-03-20
Samir - confirm Greenline security questionnaire items and send to Alyssa by 2026-03-22
next_steps: Redwood to kick off 2-week bench sprint once prompt set received
Schedule kick-off for bench run with Greenline and Redwood SEs (target week of 2026-03-30)
Send pricing/commit options for Dedicated vs Hosted tailored to observed QPS
header: Date: 2026-03-18 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~42m | Attendees: Alyssa Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Jorge Alvarez (Redwood Solutions), Dr. Priya Rao (CTO, Greenline), Ethan Morales (ML Eng), Lina Park (Platform Lead), Samir Iqbal (Security)
transcript:
[00:00] Alyssa Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining. quick roll call?
[00:05] Dr. Priya Rao: yes priya here, hi.
[00:07] Ethan Morales: ethan, hi. audio's good.
[00:09] Lina Park: lina here.
[00:12] Samir Iqbal: samir, security.
[00:14] Alyssa Chen: perfect. Marcus and I will run through a focused demo of the model catalog shortlist flow, a small bench snapshot and how the compatibility matrix surfaces runtime tradeoffs — we'll keep it tight.
[00:28] Marcus Patel: cool, i'll share my screen, bear with me. loading the catalog... okay you should see the Redwood Console catalog home, i've prefiltered for open models and the health-focused tagging.
[00:36] Ethan Morales: quick q, when you say open models, do you mean Llama variants plus some Mistral and Falcon, right?
[00:40] Marcus Patel: yeah mostly. our catalog tag "open" includes Mistral, Falcon, Llama2/3 forks, and curated quantized variants we ship with performance profiles. sometimes names get mangled in the transcription, e g Mistral shows up as 'Mistral Labs' in notes but it's actually the upstream model.
[00:55] Alyssa Chen: one thing we want to highlight is the shortlist criteria — we've got filters for latency SLO, token cost, and compatibility tiers like 'edge-friendly', 'dedicated-only' or 'vpc-ready'. i'll click the shortlist action here; you can create a shortlist from filters or from a benchmarking result.
[01:12] Dr. Priya Rao: for us latency is important for triage flows, but cost is also critical across the board — greenline processes millions of short requests. we need something in the 50-150ms per-request range at 512 tokens ideally, and ability to fall back to a cheaper model during spikes.
[01:30] Marcus Patel: makes sense. in the compatibility matrix view you'll see per-model rows with kernel mapping, quantization level, recommended GPU families, and a predicted p50/p95 latency for common seq lengths. note these are estimates from our runtime profiler.
[01:44] Lina Park: can you show an example?
[01:46] Marcus Patel: yeah picking 'Shortlist: Health-triage' — here's Mistral-2-7B-quant and Falcon-7B-int8. Mistral shows lower p50 but slightly higher memory per-request due to attention pattern. Falcon has a lower memory envelope but p95 tails worse.
[02:05] Ethan Morales: does the console show KV cache behavior? our use case will use caching heavily for repeated context.
[02:09] Marcus Patel: yes, we show KV cache hit impact estimates and a prefix cache column; also caching interacts with batch sizing so you'll see two columns: optimistic cost with cache hits and conservative cost without cache.
[02:20] Alyssa Chen: i'm going to open the bench snapshot tab — we ran a 2-hour microbench previously on a sample prompt set that looks similar to your triage examples, linked in the notes: https://redwood.app/bench/GLH-sample-2026-03. you'll see tokens/sec, latency distribution and quality metrics like exact match / hallucination proxies.
[02:40] Dr. Priya Rao: i clicked the link — good to see the hallu metrics, though sometimes those heuristics are noisy. how do you recommend we set the quality thresholds?
[02:48] Marcus Patel: great point. we usually recommend an initial quality band: generate 10k tokens and measure intent-preservation and hallucination rate on a manually labeled subset. threshold depends on your tolerance, e g 98% intent match for triage, 95% for summarization. we also surface regressions when we swap quantization.
[03:07] Ethan Morales: are the benchmarks run on dedicated pools or hosted instances? curious about variance.
[03:12] Alyssa Chen: the bench snapshot has metadata — this run was on a Dedicated T4 pool and a hosted A100 variant; we show both to compare. in your case, given cost sensitivity and throughput, we'd likely recommend a mixed routing policy: low-latency requests to Dedicated, bulk/background to hosted cheaper variants, with autoscaler for bursts.
[03:33] Samir Iqbal: security question — if we route between hosted and dedicated, where does the data live? we need to ensure PHI never leaves our VPC for certain flows.
[03:42] Alyssa Chen: absolutely, that's where Redwood Private and routing policies help. you can mark routes as 'VPC-only' and pin model variants to private runtime; fallback policies can be restricted. we'll flag the catalog rows that are 'vpc-ready' — you'll see a shield icon.
[03:58] Lina Park: when you say pin model variants, is that at the customer level so it's consistent across rollouts?
[04:02] Marcus Patel: yes, version pinning happens at the deployment config. you can roll forward with canary percentages or A/B by route. the console shows model version history and a rollback button.
[04:12] Dr. Priya Rao: can you show the compatibility matrix for on-prem? we have some legacy infra and want to know if quantized variants are stable.
[04:20] Marcus Patel: toggling 'On-prem' row here — for 4-bit quantized variants we recommend specific kernel builds; the matrix marks whether a CPU-only or GPU-accelerated runtime is supported. note: extreme quantization sometimes reduces output quality for long-context tasks.
[04:36] Ethan Morales: what's the typical quality delta from fp16 to 4-bit quant for these models?
[04:40] Marcus Patel: it varies by model and task. for instruction-following triage prompts we often see a 1-3% drop in intent match on 4-bit for some Lla-variants, but Mistral quant tends to preserve better on shorter contexts. the bench snapshot table has a 'delta_vs_fp16' column.
[04:58] Alyssa Chen: i'm going to demo the shortlist export — you can export candidate models to a bench sprint template which includes config for batch size, KV cache settings, token limit, and prompts. i'll export 'Shortlist: Health-triage' now.
[05:12] Marcus Patel: exported. sharing link to bench template: https://redwood.app/bench/template/health-triage-quickstart. this template pre-sets sequence lengths, batch targets and suggested GPU families.
[05:26] Dr. Priya Rao: we have a regulatory constraint that logs must be stored for seven years for audit — how does Redwood handle long-term logs and PII/PHI redaction?
[05:36] Samir Iqbal: (interjecting) yeah and we need KMS-managed keys for encryption at rest.
[05:40] Alyssa Chen: good questions. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and audit logs retention in your storage account. for hosted mode there's an add-on for extended audit retention. we can redact transcripts at ingestion and offer token-level pseudonymization rules. i'll attach our security pack in the follow-up.
[05:55] Ethan Morales: about the routing policy — you mentioned automatic fallback to compatible variants. how do you ensure semantic equivalence when falling back to a cheaper model?
[06:03] Marcus Patel: we don't claim full semantic equivalence. instead we provide quality gates: if a cheap variant fails a quick intent classifier or confidence threshold, the policy can route to a higher-quality model or mark the request for reprocessing. the console lets you configure thresholds per route.
[06:18] Lina Park: can we see an example routing rule?
[06:20] Marcus Patel: sure — open 'Routing policies' tab. here's a policy: route priority = Dedicated Mistral-quant -> Hosted Falcon-int8 -> Dedicated Falcon-fp16; fallback condition = p(exact match) < 0.9 or latency > 250ms. there's also traffic split and canary weights.
[06:37] Dr. Priya Rao: that latency threshold is higher than we want; suggest 150ms for triage. how does that affect cost?
[06:44] Alyssa Chen: lowering latency SLO pushes more traffic to lower-latency Dedicated pools, which increases committed capacity and cost. the console has a cost estimator that projects monthly token spend and committed instance hours given target SLO.
[06:58] Marcus Patel: i'll pull the cost estimator for your shortlist with an assumed 10k QPS profile. see the cost / latency curve chart — at 150ms p95 we estimate X dollars, at 250ms p95 it's Y dollars.
[07:12] Ethan Morales: can that output be exported to CSV? our finance team will want line items.
[07:15] Marcus Patel: yes exportable; the bench report and cost estimator both have CSV export.
[07:20] Jorge Alvarez: (adds) and we can also provide a pro forma for Dedicated commits if you want pricing bands.
[07:25] Samir Iqbal: one more security question: SSO and RBAC integration — we use SAML and SCIM for provisioning.
[07:31] Alyssa Chen: Redwood Console supports SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning plus granular RBAC. we can set route-level permissions so only platform lead or specific services can change model pinning.
[07:42] Lina Park: good. show us how to annotate a model with a compliance tag like 'HIPAA-approved'.
[07:47] Marcus Patel: clicking into the model details, there's a tags section. you can add 'HIPAA-allowed' and an audit note. we also surface a compliance readiness score based on your infra choices.
[07:59] Dr. Priya Rao: in the catalog i see a column for 'kernel compatibility' — how deep is that mapping? does it list exact CUDA/cuDNN versions?
[08:08] Marcus Patel: it lists recommended kernel families, minimum driver versions, and known optimizations like flash attention variants. for Private/on-prem we include a binary compatibility note. sometimes transcription turns CUDA into 'CuD-A' in auto-notes, apologies.
[08:23] Ethan Morales: can you run a quick simulated bench with our prompts? i know it's a live demo so maybe a micro-run.
[08:29] Marcus Patel: i can run a 3-minute microbench on one model now. i'll select Mistral-2-7B-quant from the shortlist and run sample workload 'triage-short'. starting microbench...
[08:38] Alyssa Chen: while that runs i'll highlight the quality panel — for each run we include per-prompt failure reasons like hallucination, truncation, and timeout.
[08:46] [08:46] Microbench running... (system noises)
[08:50] Marcus Patel: results coming in: p50 42ms, p95 120ms on Dedicated T4, tokens/sec 580, token cost estimated at $0.00009 per token equivalent.
[09:02] Ethan Morales: 120ms p95 looks promising. what's the variance over longer runs?
[09:06] Marcus Patel: we usually see a 10-20% p95 inflation under sustained burst traffic due to KV cache warmup; the bench template includes a warmup phase.
[09:17] Lina Park: about fallback policies — if we fallback to hosted variants, do we get tracing and end-to-end observability?
[09:23] Alyssa Chen: yes, Redwood Console shows end-to-end traces across routes and models, including route-level latency breakdown and token-level cost. traces can be exported to your APM via trace hooks.
[09:34] Dr. Priya Rao: okay, can you show an example of a regression alert? we want to prevent quality regressions post-deploy.
[09:39] Marcus Patel: sure, 'Quality monitors' tab. here's an example alert: when intent-preservation drops by 2% on the control prompt set or hallucination rate rises by >1.5% vs baseline, trigger alert to slack #glh-ml and open a rollback playbook. you can tie alerts to automatic canary rollback.
[09:59] Ethan Morales: very useful. for the bench sprint we plan to compare three models across fp16 and 4-bit quant. i'm worried about evaluation noise — any tips?
[10:07] Marcus Patel: separate runs by seed, use a stable labeled subset for quality, and measure both automated heuristics and human review on a small sample. also lock runtime configs like temp, max tokens, and ensure same tokenizer.
[10:22] Alyssa Chen: i'll note that Marcus will provide a bench template and we'll need your prompt set. Ethan, you mentioned you'd share 20-30 prompts earlier?
[10:29] Ethan Morales: yes we'll export a quick set, but we'll need guidance on anonymization before sharing.
[10:33] Samir Iqbal: Samir again — regarding anonymization, can Redwood run the bench inside our VPC so we never upload raw prompts?
[10:40] Marcus Patel: yes, Private deployment bench is supported. we can run the entire bench inside your VPC or on-prem runner, and return aggregated metrics. there's a config toggle in the bench template.
[10:51] Jorge Alvarez: adding: we can also do hybrid where raw prompts stay in your VPC and only metric summaries leave.
[10:57] Dr. Priya Rao: do you have an SLA for bench runs and turnaround time?
[11:01] Alyssa Chen: bench sprint turnaround depends on queue but for pilot customers we prioritize within 48 hours for microbenches, 3-5 days for full 2-week sprints to schedule resources.
[11:11] Marcus Patel: microbench results posted to the console; it's here in the run history. i'll jump to the compatibility matrix where we compare these models across kernels and show a tiebreaker score based on your weighted criteria (latency 40%, cost 35%, quality 25%).
[11:29] Lina Park: can we edit the weights? our product team might weigh quality higher.
[11:33] Marcus Patel: editable slider; here's a live recalculation — if quality becomes 50% weight, Mistral jumps ahead of Falcon for your shortlist. i'll capture a screenshot.
[11:43] Alyssa Chen: quick note on observability — we also provide token-level cost breakouts by model and by route for the last 30 days, which helps forecasting. we'll include that in the follow-up deck.
[11:54] Dr. Priya Rao: good. any caveats about open-model licensing we should be aware of?
[11:59] Marcus Patel: model licenses vary; we flag models in the catalog with license notes and IP warnings. for commercial use some forks require attribution or additional compliance. we'll include a license summary for each shortlisted model.
[12:11] Ethan Morales: how do you handle tokenizer differences between model families when comparing quality?
[12:16] Marcus Patel: we normalize prompts using the model tokenizer and report token-length normalized metrics. differences in subword tokenization are surfaced in a 'tokenization delta' column.
[12:26] Alyssa Chen: time check, we've got ~30 minutes left in the call, but i want to walk through a hypothetical pilot plan and responsibilities.
[12:33] Marcus Patel: pilot plan: week 0 kickoff and prompt handoff, week 1 microbench and config tuning, week 2 full bench across selected models and quality review. deliverables: bench report, cost model, recommended shortlist for production.
[12:48] Dr. Priya Rao: timeline works. resource ask?
[12:50] Alyssa Chen: we'll need your prompt set and a point person for redaction/anonymization. Redwood will supply bench template and SE time for tuning (up to 8 hours included in pilot). any concerns?
[13:04] Samir Iqbal: data residency compliance and KMS integration steps — we'll need docs.
[13:09] Alyssa Chen: will send Security pack and KMS integration checklist after the call.
[13:14] Ethan Morales: ok i'll prepare the prompt set. one quick technical question — for long context summarization, do you recommend KV cache warm start or full context replay? we have some 8k cases.
[13:23] Marcus Patel: for 8k we'd recommend warm start of KV cache where possible; replaying full context is expensive. the console shows estimated cache size and hit rates per model. for very long contexts we often prefer larger models that manage context more gracefully.
[13:36] Dr. Priya Rao: final q: do you have examples of customers who run similar health triage workloads?
[13:41] Alyssa Chen: we have anonymized case studies in the deck; i'll share references. one healthcare customer used mixed routing and saved 30% cost while maintaining p95 below 180ms.
[13:54] Marcus Patel: quick demo end note — i'll show the diff view where you can compare two bench runs side-by-side; here's Mistral fp16 vs Mistral 4-bit. differences highlighted in red for regressions.
[14:08] Ethan Morales: nice. can we automate regression tests on each model rollout?
[14:12] Marcus Patel: yes, integrate our eval webhook to CI so each model build triggers a small harness and quality gates.
[14:19] Alyssa Chen: closing recap: Redwood to send security pack, bench template, and pricing options. Greenline to send prompt set and anonymization plan. Schedule bench kick-off week of 2026-03-30.
[14:33] Dr. Priya Rao: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[14:35] Lina Park: thanks.
[14:36] Ethan Morales: thanks team.
[14:37] Samir Iqbal: bye.
[14:38] Alyssa Chen: thanks, we'll follow up with materials and next steps. bye.
notes: Security pack promised in follow-up; KMS/HSM and VPC bench options discussed
Exportable cost estimator and CSVs available
